injuryReport.name: Kenneth Walker III
factors: Officially ruled Out on weekly game status report
injuryReport.beatComment: Though Walker was able to log a limited practice Tuesday, he was listed as a non-participant Wednesday and will wind up missing a third straight contest while he continues to nurse a sore groin. With Walker sidelined, rookie Emmett Johnson is set for another turn as the Chiefs' lead back, with Jaydn Ott serving as his top backup and Nate Carter a possible practice-squad elevation. Given that the Chiefs on are on a short week, Walker -- who last saw game action Nov. 8 -- will have added time to heal before the team's next contest Dec. 3 against the Rams.
injuryReport.longComment: Buffalo Bills won’t face Chiefs star running back Kenneth Walker on Thanksgiving. The injury that has kept Kenneth Walker out of the Chiefs’ past two games continues to linger, as he’s been ruled out of Kansas City’s monumental showdown against the Buffalo Bills on Thanksgiving. Jordan Schultz was first on the major news.
injuryReport.shortComment: Buffalo Bills won’t face Chiefs star running back Kenneth Walker on Thanksgiving. The injury that has kept Kenneth Walker out of the Chiefs’ past two games continues to linger, as he’s been ruled out of Kansas City’s monumental showdown against the Buffalo Bills on Thanksgiving. Jordan Schultz was first on the major news.

injuryReport.name: Trey Smith
injuryReport.beatComment: Smith has logged two consecutive full practices, and while Smith is in the league's concussion protocol, head coach Andy Reid said Tuesday that he anticipates that Smith will be available for Thursday's game against the Bills, per Sam McDowell of The Kansas City Star. If he's cleared to play Thanksgiving Day, Smith would likely reclaim his starting job at right guard while Mike Caliendo reverts to a depth role.

injuryReport.name: Rashee Rice
injuryReport.beatComment: Rice tied for the team lead in receptions and finished as the runner-up in targets to Travis Kelce. The veteran receiver averaged a modest 8.8 yards per catch, his third game in the last four with under 10.0 yards per reception. Rice has at least five catches in four consecutive contests heading into Thursday's Week 12 Thanksgiving showdown against the Bills in Buffalo.

injuryReport.name: Patrick Mahomes
injuryReport.beatComment: Mahomes was clicking early against the Cardinals' defense, capping off the opening possession of the game with an eight-yard touchdown toss to Travis Kelce. The prolific signal-caller went on to add a 22-yard scoring pass to Kelce shortly before the end of the first half, and he capped off his day with an 18-yarder to Xavier Worthy on which the speedy receiver raced up the right sideline and into the end zone. Mahomes now has consecutive 300-yard efforts and has accomplished the feat in three of the past four games overall, affording him plenty of momentum heading into a Week 12 showdown with Josh Allen and the Bills on Thanksgiving night.

injuryReport.name: Noah Gray
injuryReport.beatComment: Though Gray was listed as a full participant on both Tuesday and Wednesday's injury reports, the Chiefs' TE2 will nonetheless carry a 'questionable" designation ahead of Week 12 action. With a 10/211/1 receiving line through 10 contests thus far, Gray is only an option in the deepest of fantasy formats, at least as long as Travis Kelce is available.

irReserve.name: Ben VanSumeren
factors: On Injured Reserve — 21-day practice window not yet opened
irReserve.beatComment: VanSumeren didn't practice Tuesday due to a sprained knee that will now keep him out for at least the next four weeks, according to Matt McMullen of the Chiefs' official site. In six regular-season games in 2026, the fourth-year pro played a majority of his reps on special teams, with just six of 104 total snaps coming on offense.

irReserve.name: Jared Wiley
factors: On Injured Reserve — 21-day practice window not yet opened
irReserve.beatComment: Wiley was carted to the locker room in the first quarter of the Chiefs' Week 10 win over the Falcons with an ankle injury. The tight end will now be on IR as he nurses his fractured ankle until at least the latter part of the regular season. Travis Kelce, Noah Gray and Jake Briningstool are now the only tight ends on the Chiefs' active roster.

coachingMatchup.headline: Joe Brady & DC Jim Leonhard vs. HC Andy Reid, OC Eric Bieniemy & DC Steve Spagnuolo (Highmark Stadium)
coachingMatchup.summary: Week 12 two-sided coordinator chess match pitting Buffalo Bills's staff (Joe Brady, OC Pete Carmichael Jr., DC Jim Leonhard) against Kansas City Chiefs (8-2)—testing both Buffalo's offensive efficiency and its defensive pass-rush and coverage discipline.
bullets: Pass-Game Efficiency & Coverage Shell Delta: Joe Brady and OC Pete Carmichael Jr. pair condensed splits with pre-snap jet motion and orbit motion to stress Kansas City Chiefs's single-high vs. two-high rotations—widening curl/flat defenders to attack the honey-hole between hook/curl linebackers and deep safeties on play-action choice/dagger concepts.

Trench Run-Fit & Two-Way Leverage: Against Kansas City Chiefs's pin-and-pull, counter, and duo runs targeting the A- and B-gaps, DC Jim Leonhard balances four-man pressure with disguised Quarters and Cover 6 split-safety rotations on early downs and in the red zone.

Money-Down & Red-Zone Execution: Third-down conversion discipline and red-zone touchdown rate govern whether Buffalo sustains multi-play scoring drives or yields momentum to Kansas City Chiefs's pass rush and coverage disguises.
Tempo, Turnovers & Venue Leverage: Highmark Stadium situational play-calling, penalty margin, and turnover differential provide the clearest late-game swing factors for both coaching staffs.

keyMatchupsMatrix.unitMatchup: Josh Allen, Dawson Knox & Keon Coleman vs. CB Nohl Williams & LB Drue Tranquill
keyMatchupsMatrix.statComparison: BUF: #12 Pass Off (241.6 yds) · #4 Off. Scoring (+8.42) | KC: #6 Pass Def (-2.69)
keyMatchupsMatrix.tacticalDetail: Josh Allen, Dawson Knox & Keon Coleman attack the intermediate seams and middle-of-the-field leverage windows against Kansas City Chiefs's #6 pass defense (-2.69). Winning early-down timing throws keeps Buffalo's offense ahead of the chains and punishes disguised single-high rotations.
keyMatchupsMatrix.filmTell: Watch Josh Allen (#17) scanning Chiefs's deep safeties at the snap—when LB Drue Tranquill widens to take away the crossers, the intermediate seam opens immediately for Dawson Knox (#88).

keyMatchupsMatrix.unitMatchup: Deone Walker, Ed Oliver & T.J. Sanders vs. QB Patrick Mahomes & OT Kahlil Benson
keyMatchupsMatrix.statComparison: BUF: #16 Def Sacks (2.3/gm) | KC: #16 Pass Protection (6.5%)
keyMatchupsMatrix.tacticalDetail: Deone Walker, Ed Oliver & T.J. Sanders lead Buffalo's #16 NFL pass rush (2.3/gm) against Kansas City Chiefs's #16 pass-protection unit (6.5%). Collapsing the interior pocket without sending extra blitzers lets Bills keep seven defenders in coverage.
keyMatchupsMatrix.filmTell: On 3rd-and-6+, watch whether Deone Walker (#96) draw chip help from Chiefs's tight ends or backs—creating 1-on-1 rush lanes inside for Ed Oliver (#91).

keyMatchupsMatrix.unitMatchup: Amani Hooker, Cole Bishop & Christian Benford vs. WR Rashee Rice & QB Patrick Mahomes
keyMatchupsMatrix.statComparison: BUF: #7 Pass Def (-1.36) | KC: #4 Pass Off (262.7 yds)
keyMatchupsMatrix.tacticalDetail: Amani Hooker, Cole Bishop & Christian Benford anchor Buffalo's #7 pass defense (-1.36) against WR Rashee Rice and Kansas City Chiefs's #4 passing attack (262.7 yds). Limiting explosive 20+ yard chunk plays forces Chiefs into sustained red-zone drives.
keyMatchupsMatrix.filmTell: Track Amani Hooker (#22) at the top of routes against WR Rashee Rice: press-bail alignment with safety help over the top takes away QB Patrick Mahomes's preferred isolation shots.

keyMatchupsMatrix.unitMatchup: James Cook III & Khalil Shakir vs. Chiefs Front Seven & LB Drue Tranquill
keyMatchupsMatrix.statComparison: BUF: #2 Rush Off (146.9 yds) | KC: #5 Rush Def (-1.76)
keyMatchupsMatrix.tacticalDetail: James Cook III & Khalil Shakir test Kansas City Chiefs's #5 run defense (-1.76) with horizontal stretch and interior cutback lanes. Generating 4.5+ yards on first down unlocks play-action explosives and neutralizes Chiefs's pass-rush packages.
keyMatchupsMatrix.filmTell: Watch whether Chiefs's linebackers over-pursue motion to the perimeter—opening decisive backside B-gap cutback lanes for James Cook III (#4).

keyMatchupsMatrix.unitMatchup: O'Cyrus Torrence, Alec Anderson & Dion Dawkins vs. DE George Karlaftis & Chiefs Simulated Pressures
keyMatchupsMatrix.statComparison: BUF: #16 Pass Protection (6.0%) | KC: #16 Def Sacks (2.4/gm)
keyMatchupsMatrix.tacticalDetail: O'Cyrus Torrence, Alec Anderson & Dion Dawkins protect Josh Allen (#16 protection at 6.0%) against DE George Karlaftis and Kansas City Chiefs's #16 pass rush (2.4/gm). Passing off interior twists and simulated blitzes cleanly determines late-down conversion efficiency.
keyMatchupsMatrix.filmTell: Watch O'Cyrus Torrence (#64) on obvious passing downs—if DE George Karlaftis cannot win clean around the arc, Chiefs must dial up interior stunts that stress Alec Anderson (#70).
